column2: Whisk the egg, oats, apple and cinnamon if using until smooth; leave for 5 minutes.
Break into soft pieces the child can hold.
Keep leftovers in a closed container in the fridge for 2 days; reheat only once.
Grate the courgette and squeeze out the liquid well with your hands; the patties won't fall apart.
Knead the minced chicken, courgette, oats and egg yolk; wash your hands after touching raw chicken.
With wet hands, form small flat patties and arrange them on the tray.
Bake for 18 minutes, turning halfway.
Chicken must reach 74°C inside; cut a patty in half: no pink inside and the juices should run clear.
Rest on the tray for 5 minutes to cool.
Boil the pasta in unsalted boiling water 2 minutes longer than the packet says, until soft enough to crush with a finger.
Add the broccoli to the same pan for the last 6 minutes of the pasta.
Drain, and while hot add the butter and cheese and stir until the cheese melts.
Break the broccoli into small pieces.
Hard cheese and curd cheese must be made from pasteurised milk; soak salty cheese in water for 1 hour to remove salt.
Put the oats and milk in a small pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 5 minutes until the oats are soft.
Remove from the heat and cool for 5 minutes.
Mash the banana with a fork and stir into the oats.
Top with the yoghurt and serve.
Don't add sugar; let the sweetness come from ripe fruit.
Peel the tomato, remove the seeds and chop finely.
Whisk the egg and milk; add the tomato.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low heat; pour in the mixture.
Cook covered for 3–4 minutes until the top is completely set.
Sprinkle with the cheese and fold in half; cook for 1 more minute.
When lukewarm, cut into strips.
Peel the carrot and potato and chop them small.
Put the lentils, vegetables and water in a pan and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Blend; if too thick, add hot water.
Don't add salt; children aged 1–3 should have no more than 2 g of salt a day, and cheese and tomato paste already contain salt.
Grate the courgette and squeeze out the liquid well with your hands.
Mix the courgette, egg, flour, curd cheese and finely chopped dill.
Drop small rounds onto the tray with a spoon and press lightly.
Bake for 20 minutes until lightly golden on top and firm in the middle.
Wash the peach, peel it and remove the stone.
Chop into small pieces the child can chew easily.
Add the honey and stir.
Honey may only be given to children who have turned 1; no more than 1 teaspoon a day.
Chop the carrot small; wash and drain the bulgur.
Melt the butter in a small pan and stir-fry the carrot and peas for 3 minutes.
Add the bulgur and water; when it boils, cook covered over low heat for 12 minutes.
Turn off the heat, put a paper towel under the lid and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Crush or quarter round, firm foods (such as peas, chickpeas and grapes).
Whisk the egg, flour, milk, apple and cinnamon until smooth; leave for 5 minutes.
Pour in a ladle of batter and tilt the pan to spread it; when golden underneath, turn and cook 1 more minute.
Roll up the crepes and cut into small pieces the child can hold.
Melt the butter in a small pan and stir the rice in it for 1 minute.
Add the chicken stock and peas; when it boils, cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Finely shred the boiled chicken and add it; turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.
Steam the salmon in the basket for 8–10 minutes.
Soften the courgette in a pan with 1 spoonful of water for 2 minutes.
Mix the pasta, flaked salmon and courgette.
When lukewarm, add the yoghurt and serve; yoghurt added to hot food will curdle.
Mash the boiled potatoes smooth with a fork while hot.
When lukewarm, add the cheese, egg yolk and flour and knead.
Make walnut-sized balls, arrange on the tray and press lightly.
Bake for 20 minutes until lightly golden underneath.
Squeeze the boiled spinach well and chop very finely.
Whisk the egg, flour, milk and spinach until smooth; leave for 5 minutes.
Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it; when cooked underneath, turn and cook 1 more minute.
Roll up and cut into small pieces.
Peel the carrots and cut finger-thick sticks long enough for the child to hold.
Toss with olive oil and cumin and arrange spaced out on the tray.
Bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway.
Stay with your child while eating; they should sit upright and not eat while walking or running.
Wash the lentils and cook them with 1 glass of water for 15 minutes until they break down.
Turn off the heat and add the bulgur; leave covered for 15 minutes to swell.
Add the tomato paste, olive oil and finely chopped parsley.
When lukewarm, knead for 3–4 minutes; if too soft, add 1 spoonful of bulgur and wait 5 minutes.
Make small flat patties that fit in the child's palm.
Drain and stir in the butter while hot.
Add the yoghurt once the pasta is lukewarm; added while hot, the yoghurt will curdle.
If you like, sprinkle a very little dried mint on top.
Soak the dried apricots in warm water for 30 minutes and drain.
Chop the apricots very finely.
Knead with the oats and tahini; if dry, add 1 spoonful of water.
Make hazelnut-sized balls and flatten them in your palm; round balls can get stuck in the throat.
Because of sesame allergy, if giving tahini for the first time start with a small amount and watch.
Keep in a closed container in the fridge for 3 days.
Dice the meat small and trim off fat and sinew.
Dice the potato, carrot and courgette small and add them; cook for 20 more minutes.
Shred the meat finely; no pink should remain inside.
Mash lightly with a fork instead of blending; this develops chewing skills.
Preheat the oven to 175°C; line a small loaf tin with baking paper.
Mash ripe bananas with brown-speckled skins with a fork.
Add the egg and olive oil and whisk.
Add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon and mix just until combined; overmixing makes the cake tough.
Pour into the tin and bake for 35 minutes; a toothpick inserted in the middle should come out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the tin, then completely on a wire rack.
Keep in a closed container for 2 days, or slice and freeze for 1 month.
Knead the cooked quinoa, carrot, egg and oats; leave for 10 minutes.
Bake for 20 minutes, turning halfway.
Peel and grate the apple.
Mix the oats, apple, milk and cinnamon in a small ovenproof dish.
Bake for 20 minutes until lightly golden on top and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes; the centre stays very hot.
Drain the boiled broccoli and chop very finely.
Mix the broccoli, cheese, egg and breadcrumbs; leave for 5 minutes.
Make walnut-sized balls and flatten them slightly.
Split the white part of the leek lengthways and wash between the layers well; slice finely.
Peel the potato and dice it small.
Melt the butter in a pan and soften the leek for 3 minutes.
Add the potato and water; when it boils, cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Blend; add the milk and heat for 1 minute without boiling.
Chop the broccoli finely and boil for 6 minutes.
Mix the drained pasta and broccoli with the butter.
Add the cheese and stir while hot until it melts.
Knead the minced chicken, courgette and oats; leave for 5 minutes.
With wet hands, form small patties and arrange on the tray; bake for 18 minutes.
Wash the courgette and dice it small.
Put the bulgur, courgette and water in a pan and bring to the boil.
Cook covered over low heat for 12 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes.
When lukewarm, serve with yoghurt.
Steam the sea bass in the basket for 8 minutes.
Mash the fish with the boiled potato using a fork and add the dill.
Make small flat patties and arrange on the tray; bake for 15 minutes until lightly golden on top.
Wash the lentils; chop the courgette and carrot small.
Cook over low heat, stirring now and then, for 20 minutes.
